questions.s: Derivatives of the first pharyngeal arch include:
o: Stapes

The stapes comes from the second arch.
The first arch gives the malleus and incus. (Last's p. 529)
Stylohyoid ligament

The stylohyoid ligament comes from the second arch.
So do the styloid process and lesser horn of the hyoid. (Last's p. 465)
Posterior belly of digastric

Posterior digastric is a second-arch muscle, supplied by VII.
Each arch muscle keeps its arch nerve. (Last's p. 634)
Anterior belly of digastric

Anterior digastric is a first-arch muscle, supplied by V3 (nerve to mylohyoid).
So the two bellies have different nerves. (Last's p. 634)

questions.s: Concerning the third and fourth pharyngeal arches:
o: Stylopharyngeus is a third-arch muscle

It is the only muscle of the third arch.
So it is supplied by IX. (Last's p. 637)
The lesser horn of the hyoid comes from the third arch

The lesser horn comes from the second arch.
The third gives the greater horn and lower body. (Last's p. 465)
The nerve of the third arch is the vagus

The nerve of the third arch is the glossopharyngeal.
The vagus serves the fourth and sixth arches. (Last's p. 627)
Cricothyroid is a third-arch muscle

Cricothyroid is a fourth-arch muscle, supplied by the superior (external) laryngeal nerve.
Other laryngeal muscles are sixth arch. (Last's p. 484)
The palatine tonsil comes from the first pouch

The palatine tonsil comes from the second pouch.
The first pouch forms the middle ear. (Last's)
The inferior parathyroid comes from the fourth pouch

The inferior parathyroid comes from the third pouch, with the thymus.
It migrates further down than the superior one. (Last's)
The thymus comes from the second pouch

The thymus comes from the third pouch.
It descends into the superior mediastinum. (Last's)
The first pouch forms the tympanic cavity and auditory tube

The first pouch forms the tubotympanic recess.
The first cleft forms the external acoustic meatus. (Last's p. 526)

questions.s: Derivatives of the neural crest include the:
o: Dorsal root ganglia

Sensory ganglion cells of spinal nerves come from neural crest.
So do those of cranial sensory ganglia, in part. (Last's)
Sympathetic ganglia

Postganglionic autonomic neurons come from neural crest.
This includes enteric neurons. (Last's)
Adrenal medulla

The medullary chromaffin cells come from neural crest.
They behave like postganglionic neurons. (Last's)
Schwann cells

Schwann cells come from neural crest.
Oligodendrocytes come from the neural tube. (Last's)
Autonomic cells lie nearest the sulcus limitans, somatic cells further away

In both alar and basal laminae, visceral (autonomic) cells lie near the sulcus limitans.
Body wall and limb (somatic) cells lie further away. (Last's p. 627)
The alar plate forms motor neurons

The alar plate is sensory; the basal plate is motor.
This is why sensory nuclei lie lateral in the brainstem. (Last's p. 627)
The sulcus limitans separates the roof plate from the floor plate

It separates the alar plate from the basal plate.
It is still visible in the floor of the fourth ventricle. (Last's p. 627)
The anterior horn develops from the alar plate

The anterior (ventral) horn comes from the basal plate.
The posterior horn comes from the alar plate. (Last's p. 627)

questions.s: Concerning the structure and supply of peripheral nerves:
o: Endoneurium surrounds each individual nerve fibre

Endoneurium wraps each fibre; perineurium groups fibres into fascicles.
Epineurium binds the fascicles into one nerve. (Last's)
Perineurium binds the fascicles into a single nerve

That is the epineurium.
Perineurium surrounds each fascicle. (Last's)
Large nerves have no nerve supply of their own

Large nerves have their own small nerves, the nervi nervorum, in their connective tissue.
These make nerve trunks sensitive to pressure. (Last's)
The phrenic nerve is supplied by regional arteries along its course in the mediastinum

It has no regional artery there, so it takes its own, the pericardiacophrenic artery.
The artery runs with it to the diaphragm. (Last's)
